span.label: Research on AI in mathematics education clusters at the middle/high school level, which accounts for more of the reviewed studies than university or primary level.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The AI tools used in mathematics education fall into eight named types: adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring systems, chatbots, augmented reality, virtual reality, serious games, learning analytics and mathematics problem solvers.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Chatbots were the most frequently studied AI tool category in the 2019-2024 window, with virtual reality tools second.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Chatbot studies appear only at university and adult-learner level, never in school-level mathematics classrooms.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AI-driven serious games and mathematics problem-solver applications are the two least-researched categories in the corpus.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Most commercialized tools identified are pedagogical rather than generative, seventeen of them being teaching-and-learning platforms such as GeoGebra, Khan Academy and Squirrel AI.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Augmented and virtual reality technologies raise students' motivation and problem-solving skills in mathematics.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reviewed literature converges on a call for longitudinal work measuring long-term effects of AI in mathematics education on learning outcomes, motivation and educational equity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
